chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about al-qasāmah, and he said: “In all claims, the evidence is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made, except specifically in cases of bloodshed.

For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was once at Khaybar when the Anṣār lost a man from among themselves, then found him slain. The Anṣār said: So-and-so, the Jew, killed our companion. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to the claimants: “Produce two just men from other than yourselves, and I will hand him over in full retaliation; but if you do not find two witnesses, then produce a qasāmah of fifty men, and I will hand him over in full retaliation.”

They said: O Messenger of Allah, we do not have two witnesses from other than ourselves, and we dislike swearing to what we did not see. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله paid the blood-money for him from his own side.

And he said: “The blood of the Muslims has only been protected by qasāmah so that when a wicked, immoral person sees an opportunity against his enemy, the fear of qasāmah restrains him lest he be killed for it, and so he refrains from killing him. Otherwise, the one against whom the claim is made is made to swear a qasāmah of fifty men: ‘We did not kill him, nor do we know any killer’; otherwise they are liable for the blood-money when they find a slain person in their midst if the claimants do not swear.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money paid as legal compensation for killing
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: proof or evidentiary demonstration required from the claimant
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the legal procedure of repeated oaths in homicide cases
key_terms.الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ: the defendant against whom the claim is made
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: the claimant who brings the legal accusation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of al-qasāmah in murder cases according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal principle of al-qasāmah in homicide cases, making bloodshed an exception to the general rule that the claimant must produce evidence and the defendant must swear an oath. It cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله at Khaybar and shows that qasāmah serves to protect Muslim lives and deter murder when direct proof is unavailable.
